# NOTES: *A Duel* by Richard Marsh (1904, Methuen; Gutenberg 38054)

Front matter: author lists other works (Beetle, Garnered, Goddess, etc.). Two books: BOOK I "Wife" (ch I–XIV), BOOK II "The Widow" (ch XV–XXXVI).

## BOOK I: WIFE

**Ch I – The End of the Honeymoon**
- Isabel "Belle" Burney (ex-music-hall singer/dancer, "queen of song and dance") married Gregory Lamb within a month of meeting him. Stranded near Carnoustie, Forfarshire, at Mrs. Macconichie's house (Mr. M also out).
- Postman brings letter to "Mr. G. Lamb" from his mother Susan Lamb (shopkeeper, Islington): refuses money; "You'd better get your wife to keep you."
- Lamb had posed as rich; car was only hired for a fortnight. Money gone; pawned items; owe a week's rent.
- Isabel leaves at ~9pm. Earlier saw Mrs. M. holding gold coins and a tobacco jar lid. Smashes china-cupboard glass with metal paper-weight; takes canvas bag (pink tape, ~20–30 coins) from tobacco jar; hides it in bodice. Leaves her leather handbag (lost).
- Walks toward Carnoustie, lost on moor, sprains ankle at Crag Moor. Sits till dawn-ish; hears wheels.

**Ch II – An Offer of Marriage**
- Driver is Dr. David Twelves, M.D., Edinburgh, small, thin, bald, aquiline nose, deep eyes, overhanging eyebrows; drives mare; going to a dying man.
- Takes her to the house; Nannie (tall, brawny, Scots, old servant) admits them. Isabel sleeps on horsehair couch.
- Twelves offers: marry dying Cuthbert Grahame; widow's share ~£20,000. Scots law: mutual recognition suffices. Isabel: "Then I'll marry him!"

**Ch III – Whom God Hath Joined**
- Isabel gives name "Isabel Burney." Hides wedding ring in glove, tucks in waistband.
- Cuthbert Grahame: huge, bloated, red sandy hair, paralysed, rigid, eyes mostly whites. Says "Damn her ankle!", "Leave God out of it."
- Ceremony: he: "I take Isabel Burney to be my wife"; she: "I take Cuthbert Grahame… in the sight of God and man." Witnesses: Nannie, Twelves.
- Grahame has a fit; dies-seeming. Nannie carries Isabel to bedroom across landing. Isabel hides bag and glove under bolster. Nannie cuts off her boot; Isabel faints. Nannie: "Is my husband dead?" – "ask Dr. Twelves."

**Ch IV – A Second Honeymoon**
- Isabel bedridden 7 days; only Nannie attends; Twelves absent. Isabel shouts; Nannie refuses to answer. Nannie: "Am I? Then I'm reckoning that age is the only difference."
- Isabel's reasoning: bigamy (already married to Gregory Lamb); hopes to keep money secret.

**Ch V – A Conversation with the Doctor**
- Twelves visits: Grahame NOT dying; paralysed; may live years. "I mistook death's mood."
- Isabel insists she's the mistress. Twelves offers £100 to leave. She refuses ("old fox"). Twelves: "postpone your first call on your husband."
- After 8th day, goes to Grahame's room.

**Ch VI – Husband and Wife**
- Isabel sees sleeping Grahame; wants to strike him. He wakes: "Who are you?" "I'm your wife." "Damn you!" "I am." Insults each other.
- Grahame: she's a "big, bouncing, blusterous, bonny" girl, "ill-bred, ignorant, impudent and imbecile." He's 50, once handsome. Asks why she married him: "Dr. Twelves told me… twenty thousand pounds." She asks £20,000 to leave.
- Nannie appears: "Maybe you'll first be shown a thing or two yourself, my lady!"

**Ch VII – A Tug of War**
- Isabel demands Nannie's respect; Nannie insults her ("nameless besom… shameless trollop").
- Isabel punches Nannie's nose, throws her out. Fight on stairs; Nannie falls onto Twelves; Nannie's leg broken.
- Isabel orders maids Jane and Martha (raw country girls). Isabel: "I'm the mistress of this house."

**Ch VIII – The Miniature**
- Isabel searches house; takes Nannie's cash; buys clothes and trunk in small town.
- Walks woods; sees Gregory Lamb in dogcart with driver she thinks is Twelves (sees only from back).
- Grahame tells story of **Margaret Wallace**: daughter of his dear friend Wallace (Scots father, English mother); he raised her; asked her to marry him; she refused, loved another man. He says "she's the most beautiful creature in the world."
- Miniature in Russia-leather case (corn-flower blue), rim of pearls, sapphires, diamonds; hidden spring.
- Isabel removes pillow → Grahame chokes; she laughs: "It wouldn't take long to make an end of you."

**Ch IX – The Sliding Panel**
- Isabel's view: Margaret was "younger and prettier." Grahame says Margaret rejected him; he'd made will leaving all to Margaret.
- Grahame's wealth: "at least two hundred thousand pounds." Intestacy: wife gets half personal, a third real estate; rest to Crown.
- Secret hiding-place: bracket in corner on his left; take down vase; lift bracket; press boss at top of socket; slide panel up.
- Blue envelope, inscription "not to be opened till after his death." Will text: "I give and bequeath all the property of which I die possessed… to Margaret Wallace, absolutely… CUTHBERT GRAHAME. Witnesses, NANNIE FORESHAW, DAVID TWELVES, M.D., Edin."
- Written by Nannie to his dictation at table by window.
- Isabel demands £5,000 added (later says £20,000); threatens to bring her bed into room. Grahame: "I'll think it over."

**Ch X – The Girl at the Door**
- Isabel plans; sends maids out; locks front door.
- Margaret Wallace arrives (London dress; ~£ poor). Tries handle; then knocks/rings. Isabel mimics Nannie through coloured-glass panels.
- Nannie (fake) says Grahame forbade her admission; threatens gun and dogs. Margaret: "I've come all the way from London."

**Ch XI – Hot Water**
- Isabel fills two pails at hot tap, pours on Margaret from landing window; "I'll scald you again… I'll take Mr. Cuthbert's gun."
- Margaret sobs: "Oh, Nannie! Nannie!" and leaves; scald scars her neck.
- Isabel writes two wills on sheets. Will A (facsimile): everything to Margaret except £5,000 to Isabel Burney. Will B: everything to "Isabel Burney… whom I have acknowledged to be my wife… with the exception of five farthings… Margaret Wallace."
- Tells Nannie she dealt with "a dreadful man." Tells Grahame the same; he: "Perhaps it wasn't her voice I heard."

**Ch XII – Signing the Will**
- Next morning: Isabel fakes pillows, calls maids Jane and Martha as witnesses. She guides Grahame's hand; signature "Cuthbert Grahame" in big sprawling letters.
- Swaps papers; Grahame: "That's not the will I signed." Isabel: "Oh yes, it is… you get everything… Margaret gets five farthings."
- She removes pillows; he chokes; she presses his chin. Places will under pillow.

**Ch XIII – The Encounter in the Wood**
- Isabel whistles in woods; plans wealth. Meets Gregory Lamb.
- Lamb: police hunted her for stealing Mrs. Macconichie's savings; he was jailed then released. Lives on £1/week from mother in cottage on Grahame's estate. Martha Blair is daughter of his landlords.
- Isabel gives him £10 note; says go back, wait for news of Grahame's death; they will go to London together and "have a real old spree."

**Ch XIV – In Cuthbert Grahame's Room**
- Martha & Jane: "Mr. Cuthbert… dead." Twelves in room.
- Grahame choked; pillows fallen. Twelves asks if she's sure pillows were in place; suggests she dragged them.
- Isabel takes will and miniature. Twelves: "I am not likely to forget that—ever."

## BOOK II: THE WIDOW

**Ch XV – "The Gordian Knot"**
- **Harry Talfourd**: author, now secretary to Mrs. Lamb at £300/yr; gets La France roses daily from her; loves Meg (Margaret).
- Gregory Lamb (now expensively dressed) asks Talfourd to get Isabel to give £1,000 for Monte Carlo.
- Isabel visits Talfourd: has his play *The Gordian Knot* (from actor-manager **Bertram Winton**). She'll produce it and play Lady Glover (Susan Stone). Talfourd afraid of her.

**Ch XVI – Margaret is Puzzled**
- **Dorothy "Dollie" Johnson**: lady writer, friend. Margaret draws illustrations for Harry's stories; rejected.
- Margaret's photo of Grahame over mantelpiece.
- Harry: play accepted by Mrs. Lamb; he's afraid of her ("hypnotises me").
- Card: "David Twelves, M.D., Edin."

**Ch XVII – An Unexpected Visitor**
- Twelves visits Margaret (found her via magazine). Kisses her. Says he'd wanted her for wife.
- Margaret's account: Nannie refused entry and poured boiling water. Twelves: Nannie was bedridden. Margaret: "I've been acquainted with Nannie Foreshaw's voice…"
- Twelves: Mrs. Lamb is "Gregory Lamb's wife"; "I once met a Gregory Lamb… none but a fool of a woman would ever have married him."

**Ch XVIII – Cronies**
- **J. Andrew McTavish** (McTavish & Brown, Southampton Row; house Mecklenberg Square) dines with Twelves.
- Grahame's fortune: "nearer £300,000 than £200,000"; probate under £40,000.
- Isabel harasses firm: broke into office and safe; drugged McTavish with ether; claims 10,000 Hardwood Company shares (30% dividends) withheld; produced one share.
- Lawyer **Isaac Luker** (Brown's rival or associate; disreputable) helps her.
- Twelves suspects Isabel murdered Grahame; "mills of God grind slowly."

**Ch XIX – In Council**
- Margaret's sitting-room: Margaret, Dollie, Winton, Frank Staines (wealthy, loves Dollie), Harry.
- Winton: Mrs. Lamb is "fonder of Talfourd than he is of her."
- Margaret: "Let me see Mrs. Lamb." Plan: she goes to Isabel's "At Home" next evening.

**Ch XX – The Impending Sword**
- Connaught Square boudoir. Isabel demands £10,000 within a week from Luker (offers £15,000).
- Luker: shares must be proved; McTavish & Brown may go bankrupt.
- Gregory Lamb arrives; wants £1,000; Isabel has ~£50 at bank.
- Isabel: "Cuthbert Grahame… never been found"; "Since the pillow slipped from under him, I've never been the same."
- Isabel drinks ether (decanter/wineglass).
- Isabel invites Talfourd and Margaret to her At Home tonight.

**Ch XXI – Out of the Blue**
- At Home crowded: "on the make" guests.
- Margaret & Harry arrive by growler. Harry introduces Margaret.
- Isabel sees Margaret: "You can't come in!… He says you're not to—and you shan't!" She gibbers; a doctor calms her; she flees.

**Ch XXII – Margaret Settles the Question**
- Cab home. Margaret: "I believe she did mean something… I'm afraid."
- Margaret: "Never! never! never!" Lady Glover not to be played by Isabel. Winton: play shelved.
- Next morning Dollie visits; Margaret refuses to talk. Dr. Twelves calls.

**Ch XXIII – Margaret Resolves to Fight**
- Twelves brings Nannie's letter (dictated; Nannie cannot write well; leg broken; "Dear Mr. David"). Nannie denies refusing; says Isabel imitated her voice.
- Twelves confesses he brought the woman; says she murdered Grahame by pulling pillows; he testified at inquest.
- Twelves: Grahame had meant to leave Margaret fortune; Isabel tricked him into signing.
- Grahame promised Margaret "fifty thousand pounds a year."
- Margaret: "Now I understand"; she will engage "in a duel with Mrs. Gregory Lamb." Seconds: Harry and Twelves. "a duel to the death."

**Ch XXIV – The Interior**
- Morning after party. Isabel, in room, smashes furniture? (servants drunk, bottles everywhere). Rings bell; no answer.
- Butler **James Cottrell** (drunk, half-dressed): wages overdue 3 months; "I should like my overdue wages."
- Luker arrives. Isabel demands £10,000; Luker: no; suggests compromise to half. Isabel: will go to McTavish & Brown with him.

**Ch XXV – Alarums and Excursions**
- McTavish & Brown offices. **Lady Julia Dykes** (widow, Fennington Park; son Eastman to university) visiting.
- Isabel and Luker burst in; clerk **Mr. Riseley** pushed aside; Isabel locks doors, keys pocketed.
- Isabel demands £40,000 (then £25,000; £10,000 cash). Threatens with McTavish's malacca cane; Luker restrains.
- Constable called; Luker removed; Isabel leaves; "You couple of thieves!"

**Ch XXVI – Solicitor and Client**
- Luker & Isabel on street. He refuses; she says "I'm coming with you." Luker calls policeman; she leaves.
- Isabel goes to Luker's house (cul-de-sac off Stamford Street); Luker's two ruffians beat/menace her; she leaves.

**Ch XXVII – Pure Ether**
- Connaught Square: Cottrell and servants dismissed (with policeman's sovereign). Bailiffs in house (bill of sale).
- Isabel alone, hallucinating bed/Grahame in boudoir. Breaks liqueur case, drinks ether ("Here's to Isaac Luker!").
- Gregory returns; Isabel: "Gregory… in Cuthbert Grahame's bedroom."

**Ch XXVIII – Mr. Lamb in a Communicative Mood**
- Dinner at Holborn Restaurant (Twelves, Margaret, Harry). Meet drunk Gregory Lamb on street.
- Lamb tells: Isabel crammed ether down throat; described her "visions": pillows, "two wooden posts" carved on fireplace; "something I ought to understand… Cuthbert Grahame's money."
- Taken to McTavish's house (with Brown). Lamb repeats story. Margaret: "I believe… the duel has advanced another stage."

**Ch XXIX – Margaret Pays a Call**
- Margaret wears old scalded dress; visits Connaught Square; bailiff on steps.
- Isabel in bed. Margaret accuses her: bigamy, will trick, murder. Demonstrates pillows.
- Gives drawings of left-hand pillar: shaft turns; neck slides; torus hinges; cupboard behind mantelpiece (Open Sesame allusion). Says "not dare… the dead hand waiting."
- Leaves drawings with Isabel.

**Ch XXX – Mrs. Lamb in Search of Advice**
- Isabel at Luker's door (whistle signal). Claims: money found at Pitmuir, in mantelpiece; quarter-million.
- Luker suspicious; telephone installed. Isabel offers £1,000 + bond; she's frightened of Grahame's room.
- Plan: 10 o'clock train from King's Cross next morning; Luker demands return ticket.

**Ch XXXI – Mrs. Lamb Returns to Pitmuir**
- Journey; missed connection at Dundee. Arrive small roadside station, Forfarshire, 9–10pm, misty.
- Station-master rude; "Sam Harris" refuses fly; driver with cart. Driver refuses to drive to house ("Cuthbert Grahame's walking about among the trees").
- Isabel and driver quarrel; she whips and drives cart; cart overturns into ditch; driver injured.

**Ch XXXII – At the Gate**
- They walk. Luker: Margaret has "nobbled" locals; "agents" everywhere. Isabel: "This is my property."
- Gate creaks open; avenue.

**Ch XXXIII – At the Door**
- Lantern; rabbits; Luker blows at figure (lantern blown out by someone); shots fired, one scream, figure flees.
- Luker and Isabel see glowing white figure of Grahame, gasping for breath. Luker dismisses.
- Isabel: "It was Cuthbert Grahame." Luker vanishes; door opened from inside by unknown hand.

**Ch XXXIV – Towards Judgment**
- Isabel drinks ether flask on doorstep; loses senses.
- Sees Nannie on stairs; screams "I didn't kill you!"
- Climbs to Grahame's bedroom; "Cuthbert Grahame, I hear you calling—I am here." Throws open door.

**Ch XXXV – Judges**
- Luminous room. Voice (Margaret's) interrogates: "Did you murder Cuthbert Grahame?" Isabel: "Yes."
- Confesses pillows dragged, tricked will, killed him to avoid exposure.
- Present: Margaret (with lamp, wrote confession), Twelves, McTavish, Brown, Nannie (with stick), Harry.
- Margaret reads confession; Isabel signs. Isabel collapses.

**Ch XXXVI – Pleasant Dreams!**
- Isabel: certified lunatic; kept, paid for by Margaret; babbling idiot.
- Ether habit caused madness.
- Margaret found money in hidden cupboard. Married Harry Talfourd ("Mrs. Henry Talfourd"); rich; artist; funds charity.
- Harry burned *The Gordian Knot*; never wrote another play.
- Dr. Twelves lives; vows never to help strange women again.
- Nannie Foreshaw dead. McTavish & Brown thrive; Mrs. Talfourd is client.
- Gregory Lamb given passage to South Africa and money; presumed dead.
- Grahame's house now children's sanatorium/holiday home.
